text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- In Bonn nearly all parties see themselves as the winners of local election in Hessen
- Protests against nuclear waste transport. Protesters stage sit-down protests along some of the route to make it impossible for train pass
- More extreme right-wing violence in Berlin
- The European Union wants to be at forefront of environmental protection
- Carbon-dioxide emissions have increased in Germany
- Germans travel abroad more and more
HANDELSBLATT
- EMU will not be delayed Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer says. Despite the many rumours European monetary union should start on time
- Shipment of nuclear waste rolls towards Gorleben medium-term nuclear waste storage depot in northern Germany
- No drastic rise in unemployed. Reports about a new record unemployment in February are dismissed by the president of the Federal Office for Employment Bernhard Jagoda
- Paris and Bonn are agreed on European Union reform
- Deutsche Telekom shares increase in value
- Industry is divided over blanket taxation of night work, holiday work and weekend work
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Barricades block streets to Gorleben. Growing opposition to nuclear waste transportation
- Industry proposes blanket taxation of night work, weekend work and holiday work
- Pension contributions remain higher as thought
- Germans increasingly go on holiday abroad
DIE WELT
- Nuclear waste shipment rolls towards Gorleben medium-term storage depot
- Industry is ready to compromise on tax reform
- Border guards admit they killed refugee trying escape across Berlin Wall
- CDU and SPD satisfied with local election results in Hessen
